snippet.description:
Democrats just won back power in the midterms, so why was it so hard to get them to answer a simple survey about what they want to do with it?

We asked Democratic insiders four questions about the future of their party at the What’s Next summit in Denver. When almost no one responded, it raised the question: Do Democrats actually have a plan?

It depends on who you ask. US Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA) answered our survey questions in a candid conversation, where he broke down why voters haven’t necessarily fallen in love with the Democratic brand and why the party must center people over politics.

00:00 Democrats search for What’s Next
03:03 Warnock: Democrats need to prioritize people over politics
04:23 Corporate money limits what Democrats can do
06:09 Why Democrats can’t ignore the South
09:36 Mississippi’s breakthrough
12:01 Showing up matters to rural voters
13:51 Warnock on political alienation and inequality
14:47 Do Senate Dems need fresh leadership?
16:46 Warnock describes his ideological spectrum 
17:52 Islamaphobia, Israel, and what Warnock wants to see from Democrats
24:24 Is Warnock running for president?
26:06 Astead’s takeaways: Voters, not party elites, will determine Democrats’ future

Register for FREE 6-Month Prelims 2027 Strategy Webinar (22 Nov, 5 PM): https://shorturl.at/E2y2H
Explore Prelims Master Program (PMP) 2027:
https://shorturl.at/ZHr3s

Why did UPSC Prelims 2026 feel almost unsolvable? Has the nature of UPSC Prelims questions changed, and what does this mean for aspirants preparing for UPSC CSE 2027?

From unconventional factual questions and lengthy statements to application-based and reasoning questions, UPSC Prelims 2026 challenged the way aspirants approached the paper.

In this video, we analyse actual UPSC Prelims 2026 PYQs, including questions on Amur Falcons, Article 13 of the Constitution, sustainable development and Art & Culture, to understand how seemingly difficult questions can be approached through conceptual clarity and the right preparation strategy.

Learn what went wrong in Prelims 2026 and how to strengthen your UPSC Prelims 2027 preparation through fundamentals, revision, PYQ analysis and practice.

Timestamps:
00:00 – Why UPSC Prelims 2026 Felt Unsolvable
01:14 – Prelims Cutoff Trends & Paper Difficulty
03:33 – What Made UPSC Prelims 2026 Different?
09:32 – Amur Falcon PYQ: Solving Through Concepts
12:34 – Article 13 PYQ: Application-Based Questions
16:08 – Why Tips & Tricks Are Not Enough
19:49 – How to Approach Lengthy UPSC Questions
24:27 – Solving Difficult Art & Culture PYQs
26:37 – Preparing for UPSC Prelims 2027
